catalog_quote: 1.2 Phonotactics The syllable structure of Longgu is (C)V(V). ... Any pair of vowels in Longgu may appear in a vowel sequence. Any vowel, including a geminate vowel, can occur with any other vowel in the same syllable. ... 1.3 Stress Stress operates at the level of a phonological word. Primary stress is on the penultimate syllable and secondary stress is on every alternate preceding syllable.

audit.reasoning: Both deciding quotations are verbatim in copies we hold at the stated places (Hill 2002 p.539 sec. 1.3; Hill 1992 sec. 2.3). The sources are the language's reference grammar (1992 ANU thesis, 360 pp) and the author's own 2002 sketch; Glottolog lists nothing better (the 2011 Lincom book is the same grammar republished; Ivens 1934 is an older missionary sketch). I downloaded the open-access thesis PDF from ANU and read sec. 2.3 from page scan: it confirms penultimate primary stress with alternating preceding secondary stress in the phonological word, and the listed exceptions (initial long vowel; extrametrical object suffix on Class 1/2 verbs), matching the record's rule, the secondary-stress rule, word domain and 'listed-set' exceptions. The clean transcription saved beside the PDF can replace the garbled scanned exq_ text if desired, but no reclassification is indicated.

sources.quote: 'Stress operates at the level of a phonological word. Primary stress is on the penultimate syllable and secondary stress is on every alternate preceding syllable.' Phonological word = base + affixes, NP clitics, reduced deictics, inalienable possessive; alienable possessive = two stress domains. Exceptions: 'If the first syllable of a word is a long vowel, the stress does not move' (iíva, iívana); 'The object suffix on Class 1 and 2 verbs is extrametrical (i.e. it does not count for word stress)' (áde-a, wá'i-a, pítu-a).
